# Per-fixture benign-delta allowlist for the
# e2e-fidelity-compare-nlohmann-json-consumer gate.
#
# Consumer-mode fidelity diffs the consumer .o (testdata/fidelity/
# consumers/json_consumer.cpp compiled twice: once against cmake's
# installed nlohmann/json headers, once via Bazel against the
# converted :nlohmann_json cc_library that PR #268's
# lowerInterfaceLibraries lift synthesizes from the trace's
# add_library(nlohmann_json INTERFACE) call).
#
# nlohmann/json is template-heavy (basic_json + adl_serializer +
# detail::* all parameterised on the value-type tree). A single
# consumer.cpp pulls in 1000+ template instantiations + typeinfo /
# vtable / runtime-string machinery; the cmake-side build and
# Bazel-side build differ slightly per toolchain (visibility,
# inlining heuristics) so the resulting .o symbol sets diverge.
# None of the deltas are nlohmann/json *correctness* issues —
# they're all toolchain-noise inside the json template surface.
#
# Mass-allowlisting with `prefix:` (a syntax added alongside this
# gate in cmd/fidelity-compare/internal/classifier — see
# TestLoadAllowlist_PrefixEntries) suppresses every symbol in
# the nlohmann namespace + its RTTI / vtable mangling shapes.
# An operator-curated narrow prefix could be more precise; the
# broad-prefix approach keeps the allowlist file small and the
# gate signal focused on real per-target regressions.

# All basic_json template instantiations + lambdas + nested types
prefix:_ZN8nlohmann
# typeinfo / typeinfo-string / vtable for nlohmann classes
prefix:_ZTIN8nlohmann
prefix:_ZTSN8nlohmann
prefix:_ZTVN8nlohmann
# Lambdas inside basic_json::create<...> instantiations
prefix:_ZZN8nlohmann
# libstdc++ free helpers (std::forward, std::eq, std::ne,
# std::lt, std::__find_if, std::__advance, std::_Destroy,
# std::signbit, std::isfinite, std::move, std::forward, etc.)
# instantiated against json's value-type tree as template
# parameters. The Bazel-side hermetic toolchain emits these
# at .o level; the cmake-side host toolchain inlines them
# inside the basic_json template body. Pure libstdc++ /
# inlining-decision noise — no correctness signal for the
# converter.
# All non-member std::* functions (_ZSt*) — the consumer.cpp uses
# only json APIs, so any std::* symbol that appears bazel-only is a
# libstdc++ helper inlined cmake-side (std::forward, std::move,
# std::swap, std::eq/ne/lt, std::_Destroy, std::__find_if,
# std::__advance, std::signbit, std::isfinite, ...). No converter-
# regression signal can hide behind this — the consumer touches
# no std:: symbols directly.
prefix:_ZSt
# std::* member functions instantiated against json types
# (basic_string<char>, vector<json>, map<string,json>, etc.):
prefix:_ZNSt
# const std::* member functions (same coverage as _ZNSt but for
# const-qualified methods):
prefix:_ZNKSt
# const non-member std::* helpers
prefix:_ZNK
# __gnu_cxx::* (libstdc++'s extension namespace — __normal_iterator,
# __aligned_buffer, char_traits<char>, __ops::* iterator algorithms,
# eq/ne/mi operators on iterators). Same noise category as _ZSt/_ZNSt:
# inlining-decision deltas on libstdc++ helpers the consumer
# transitively pulls in through json.
prefix:_ZN9__gnu_cxx
# libstdc++ shared_ptr / make_shared machinery — std::_Sp_*
# vtable + typeinfo entries the consumer pulls in via json's
# detail::output_adapter shared_ptr usage.
_ZTISt19_Sp_make_shared_tag
_ZTVSt16_Sp_counted_baseILN9__gnu_cxx12_Lock_policyE2EE
# libstdc++ basic_string _M_construct internal _Guard scope —
# the ctor/dtor of the RAII guard that wraps string construction
# when an iterator throws. Bazel's libstdc++ emits these,
# cmake's host gcc inlines them.
prefix:_ZZNSt7__cxx1112basic_string
# Placement new + matching delete (operator new(size_t, void*)
# and operator delete(void*, void*)). Bazel-side compile emits
# these when json's basic_json constructor uses placement-new
# for its variant union.
_ZdlPvS_
_ZnwmPv
